create_annotation.description: Mark an event - a deploy, an incident, a maintenance window - on a Grafana time axis. Name a dashboard to pin it there, or leave the dashboard empty for an organisation-wide annotation that any panel querying by tag will pick up. With an end time as well it marks a region rather than a moment.
create_annotation.name: create_annotation

parameters.description: What to show on the annotation.
parameters.name: text

parameters.description: Pin the annotation to this dashboard. Leave empty for an organisation-wide one.
parameters.name: dashboard_uid

parameters.description: Pin it to one panel of that dashboard. Leave empty to put it on every panel.
parameters.name: panel_id

parameters.description: Tags to attach. Panels can be set up to show every annotation carrying a tag.
parameters.name: tags

parameters.description: When the event happened. Leave empty and Grafana stamps it with the moment the step runs.
parameters.name: from_time

parameters.description: Set this as well as the start time to mark a region rather than a single moment.
parameters.name: to_time

create_dashboard.description: Create a dashboard. It is created with no panels unless you supply a full dashboard model in Dashboard JSON, which the other fields are then laid over - Grafana's panel model is too large to fill in as form fields, so paste the JSON you already have. Returns the new dashboard's UID and URL.
create_dashboard.name: create_dashboard

parameters.description: The dashboard's name, shown in lists and search.
parameters.name: title

parameters.description: Which folder to file the dashboard in. Leave empty for the instance's General folder.
parameters.name: folder_uid

parameters.description: A UID of your own, up to 40 letters, numbers, hyphens and underscores. Leave empty and Grafana generates one.
parameters.name: uid

parameters.description: Tags to file the dashboard under.
parameters.name: tags

parameters.description: A sentence about what the dashboard is for.
parameters.name: description

parameters.description: The time zone the dashboard's times are shown in. Pick one, or type any IANA zone name such as Europe/London.
parameters.name: timezone_name

parameters.description: How often the dashboard reloads by itself.
parameters.name: refresh

parameters.description: Whether people can edit the dashboard in the Grafana UI. Off makes it read-only there; this API can still change it.
parameters.name: editable

parameters.description: A complete Grafana dashboard model to start from - the JSON behind Dashboard settings > JSON Model, or an export. The fields above are applied on top of it.
parameters.name: dashboard_json

parameters.description: A note recorded against this save, shown in the dashboard's version history.
parameters.name: message

create_folder.description: Create a folder to file dashboards and alert rules in. Give a parent folder to nest it inside another one.
create_folder.name: create_folder

parameters.description: The folder's name.
parameters.name: title

parameters.description: A UID of your own, up to 40 letters, numbers, hyphens and underscores. Leave empty and Grafana generates one.
parameters.name: uid

parameters.description: Nest the new folder inside this one. Leave empty to create it at the top level.
parameters.name: parent_uid

delete_annotation.description: Delete an annotation. This is permanent - annotations have no recycle bin.
delete_annotation.name: delete_annotation

parameters.description: The numeric ID of the annotation, as returned by 'Create annotation' or 'List annotations'.
parameters.name: annotation_id

delete_dashboard.description: Delete a dashboard. On Grafana instances with the recycle bin enabled it can be restored from Dashboards > Recently deleted for 30 days; elsewhere this is permanent.
delete_dashboard.name: delete_dashboard

parameters.description: The dashboard to act on. Paste its UID, or the dashboard's URL - the UID is the part after /d/.
parameters.name: dashboard_uid

delete_folder.description: Delete a folder and every dashboard filed in it. Grafana refuses if the folder also holds alert rules unless you tick 'Delete alert rules too', which cannot be undone.
delete_folder.name: delete_folder

parameters.description: The folder to act on. Pick one, or paste a folder UID or a folder URL.
parameters.name: folder_uid

parameters.description: Delete the folder even though alert rules live in it, deleting those rules as well. Off, Grafana refuses rather than deleting them.
parameters.name: force_delete_rules

get_dashboard.description: Read one dashboard in full: its stored model - title, description, tags, time zone, refresh interval and every panel on it - alongside Grafana's own metadata about where it is filed, who last changed it and what this connection is allowed to do to it.

dashboard.description: Request rate, error rate and latency.
dashboard.title: Production Overview

get_dashboard.name: get_dashboard

parameters.description: The dashboard to act on. Paste its UID, or the dashboard's URL - the UID is the part after /d/.
parameters.name: dashboard_uid

get_folder.description: Read one folder: its title, URL, current version, who created and last changed it, and what this connection is allowed to do to it.
get_folder.name: get_folder

parameters.description: The folder to act on. Pick one, or paste a folder UID or a folder URL.
parameters.name: folder_uid

list_alert_rules.description: Every Grafana-managed alert rule, with its title, UID, the folder and group it belongs to, its labels and annotations, and whether it is paused. These are the rules themselves, not what is firing - use 'List firing alerts' for that.
list_alert_rules.name: list_alert_rules

list_alerts.description: The alerts Grafana is holding right now - firing, silenced or inhibited - with each one's labels, summary and how long it has been in that state. This is live alert state, so an alert that has resolved is gone from it; an empty list means nothing is firing.
list_alerts.name: list_alerts

parameters.description: Include the alerts that are currently firing. On by default.
parameters.name: active

parameters.description: Include alerts a silence is holding back. On by default; turning it off leaves them out rather than showing only them.
parameters.name: silenced

parameters.description: Include alerts held back because a related alert is already firing. On by default.
parameters.name: inhibited

parameters.description: Only alerts whose labels match all of these, each written as severity="critical".
parameters.name: matchers

parameters.description: Only alerts routed to contact points whose name matches this.
parameters.name: receiver

items.description: The alerts currently firing or suppressed

list_annotation_tags.description: Every tag used on an annotation in this organisation, with how many annotations carry it. Use it to see which tags exist before filtering by one.
list_annotation_tags.name: list_annotation_tags

parameters.description: Only tags beginning with this text. Leave empty for all of them.
parameters.name: tag

parameters.description: How many tags to return. Defaults to 100.
parameters.name: limit

items.description: The tags in use, with a count each

list_annotations.description: The annotations marking events on Grafana's time axes, narrowed by dashboard, panel, tag, time range, or whether Grafana Alerting wrote them. Returns each one's ID, text, tags and times.
list_annotations.name: list_annotations

parameters.description: Only annotations on this dashboard. Leave empty for every dashboard, and for the organisation-wide ones.
parameters.name: dashboard_uid

parameters.description: Only annotations on this panel of that dashboard.
parameters.name: panel_id

parameters.description: Only annotations carrying all of these tags. Leave empty to ignore tags.
parameters.name: tags

parameters.description: Narrow to the ones people and workflows added, or to the ones Grafana Alerting wrote. Leave empty for both.
parameters.name: type_filter

options.label: Added by a person or by the API

parameters.description: Only annotations at or after this moment.
parameters.name: from_time

parameters.description: Only annotations at or before this moment.
parameters.name: to_time

parameters.description: How many to return, up to 1000. Defaults to 100.
parameters.name: limit

list_contact_points.description: The contact points Grafana Alerting delivers notifications to - email, Slack, webhooks - with each one's name, type and settings. Secret settings such as a webhook URL come back redacted.
list_contact_points.name: list_contact_points

parameters.description: Only the contact point with this exact name. Leave empty for all of them.
parameters.name: name

list_dashboard_versions.description: The saved versions of one dashboard, newest first, with who saved each one, when, and the change note they left. Use it to see what changed on a dashboard and when.
list_dashboard_versions.name: list_dashboard_versions

parameters.description: The dashboard to act on. Paste its UID, or the dashboard's URL - the UID is the part after /d/.
parameters.name: dashboard_uid

parameters.description: How many versions to return. Defaults to 20.
parameters.name: limit

parameters.description: How many of the newest versions to skip before returning any. Use it to read further back.
parameters.name: start

dashboard_uid.description: The dashboard these versions belong to

items.description: The dashboard's saved versions, newest first

list_datasources.description: Every data source in the organisation, with each one's UID, name, type and URL - the UID being what a dashboard panel or an alert rule refers to it by. Needs the service account's role to be Admin; a Viewer or an Editor is refused.
list_datasources.name: list_datasources

list_folders.description: The folders this connection can see, with each one's UID, title and URL. Give a parent folder to list the folders nested inside it instead of the top-level ones.
list_folders.name: list_folders

parameters.description: List the folders nested inside this one. Leave empty for the top-level folders.
parameters.name: parent_uid

parameters.description: How many to return per page, up to 1000. Defaults to 100.
parameters.name: limit

parameters.description: Which page to read. Defaults to the first.
parameters.name: page

search_dashboards.description: Find dashboards and folders by title, tag or folder. Returns each one's UID, title, URL, tags and the folder it is in - the UID being what every other Grafana action takes. Leave everything empty to list what the connection can see.
search_dashboards.name: search_dashboards

parameters.description: Only dashboards and folders whose title contains this text. Leave empty for all of them.
parameters.name: query

parameters.description: Only items carrying all of these tags. Leave empty to ignore tags.
parameters.name: tags

parameters.description: Narrow to dashboards or to folders. Leave empty for both.
parameters.name: type_filter

parameters.description: Only items inside these folders. Leave empty to search everywhere.
parameters.name: folder_uids

parameters.description: Only the dashboards the service account has starred.
parameters.name: starred

parameters.description: How many to return per page, up to 5000. Defaults to 50.
parameters.name: limit

parameters.description: Which page to read. Defaults to the first.
parameters.name: page

update_annotation.description: Change an existing annotation's text, tags or times. Only the fields you fill in change. Grafana answers this one with a confirmation rather than the annotation, so read it back with 'List annotations' if a later step needs its new contents.
update_annotation.name: update_annotation

parameters.description: The numeric ID of the annotation, as returned by 'Create annotation' or 'List annotations'.
parameters.name: annotation_id

parameters.description: New text for the annotation. Leave empty to keep the current text.
parameters.name: text

parameters.description: Tags to set, as a list. Replaces the existing tags rather than adding to them; leave empty to leave them alone.
parameters.name: tags

parameters.description: Move the annotation to this moment.
parameters.name: from_time

parameters.description: Move the end of the annotated region here.
parameters.name: to_time

update_dashboard.description: Change a dashboard's settings: rename it, replace its tags or description, change its time zone, auto-refresh interval or whether it can be edited in the UI, or move it to another folder. Only the fields you fill in change - the panels on the dashboard are read first and saved back untouched.
update_dashboard.name: update_dashboard

parameters.description: The dashboard to act on. Paste its UID, or the dashboard's URL - the UID is the part after /d/.
parameters.name: dashboard_uid

parameters.description: A new name for the dashboard. Leave empty to keep the current one.
parameters.name: title

parameters.description: Tags to set, as a list. Replaces the existing tags rather than adding to them; leave empty to leave them alone.
parameters.name: tags

parameters.description: A sentence about what the dashboard is for.
parameters.name: description

parameters.description: The time zone the dashboard's times are shown in. Pick one, or type any IANA zone name such as Europe/London.
parameters.name: timezone_name

parameters.description: How often the dashboard reloads by itself.
parameters.name: refresh

parameters.description: Whether people can edit the dashboard in the Grafana UI. Off makes it read-only there; this API can still change it.
parameters.name: editable

parameters.description: Move the dashboard into this folder. Leave empty to leave it where it is.
parameters.name: folder_uid

parameters.description: A note recorded against this save, shown in the dashboard's version history.
parameters.name: message

update_folder.description: Give a folder a new name. The folder's UID does not change, so every dashboard in it and every link to it still work.
update_folder.name: update_folder

parameters.description: The folder to act on. Pick one, or paste a folder UID or a folder URL.
parameters.name: folder_uid

parameters.description: The folder's new name.
parameters.name: title

description: Manage Grafana dashboards, folders and annotations, and read alert state, alert rules and data sources.
